Account.description: A provider account, by reference only (E15.1): never its secret.

config_dir.description: The harness's config dir, relative to the runner's config root (`relative_path_ok`).

credential_env.description: The variable the token goes in, one of the harness's auth variables.

credential_ref.description: The file holding the token, relative to the runner's credentials dir.

Captured.description: One output pipe: redacted UTF-8 (lossy), cut at the limit with a marker.

bytes.description: How many bytes the process wrote, kept or not.

truncated.description: `text` was cut at the limit and ends in `TRUNCATED_MARKER`.

Close.description: A stream given up. From the Core on a running command: cancel it.

Command.description: Core to runner, the first frame of a command stream.

oneOf.description: Answers `result` at once: proves the path end to end.
An op from a newer Core: answered `unsupported_command`. Never sent.
Runner to Core, the first frame of a connection, on stream 0.
Core to runner: the hello is accepted.
A type from a newer peer: ignored. Never sent.

protocol.description: The version the Core speaks on this connection.

Credit.description: Flow control: the sender of this frame accepts `bytes` more `output` bytes on the stream.

DiskReport.description: A runner's disk use (1.15, E15.9), as measured after its last clean-up pass.

caches_bytes.description: The shared build caches, one per repo (`CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, package stores, …).

full.description: Over the cap with nothing left it may evict.

mirrors_bytes.description: The bare repo mirrors, which hold every issue's branch: never evicted.

removed.description: Issues whose worktrees this pass removed: idle past the limit, or evicted for room.

worktrees.description: Each worktree it holds, oldest use first.

DriverInfo.description: A driver a runner offers (`exec` now; `pty`, `harness` later).

capacity.description: How many of its commands run at once; one more is answered `busy`.

commands.description: The command ops it takes, e.g. `noop`, `exec.run`.

ErrorCode.description: Machine codes, snake_case like the client API's (handshake spec §14).

oneOf.description: A frame or payload that does not parse, or a stream id that breaks the rules.
The peer's protocol major is not one this side speaks.
No advertised driver takes this command op.
The command's arguments are refused (e.g. a relative `cwd`).
The driver is at its advertised capacity; retry later.
The program could not be started.
The command was cancelled by a `close`.
Anything else on the runner's side.
A code from a newer peer. Never sent.

ExecLimits.description:
What the Core asks for; the runner clamps each to its own ceiling and uses its default
for an absent one.

max_output_bytes.description: The most of stdout, and of stderr, kept; the rest is dropped and marked.

timeout_ms.description: Wall clock until the process group gets TERM, then KILL.

exit_code.description: Absent when it was ended by a signal (its timeout included).

timed_out.description: It ran past its timeout and was killed.

ExecRun.description: Runs `program args…` to its end, bounded, and answers with its exit and output.

cwd.description: An absolute directory; absent, the runner's own working directory.

env.description: Variables set in the child as given.

env_pass.description:
Names of the runner's own variables to pass on. Only those also on the runner's
allow-list are; the child's environment starts empty.

payload.description: The body for `kind` (`Body`; schema `V2Payload`); absent for `heartbeat`.

oneOf.description: A kind from a newer peer: skipped. Never sent.

HostLoad.description:
The host's load when a heartbeat was sent (1.26): its one-minute load average and its CPU
count. The server stretches a loaded runner's lease by `avg1 / cores`, up to a cap.

Login.description:
A login place on a runner host (1.20): `dir` is relative to its config root
(`claude`, `accounts/claude-a`), or `credentials/<file>` for an account's token file.

harness.description: The harness, when the dir is a harness's own.

state.description: `logged_in`, `logged_out`, or `unknown` (the login lives in the keychain).

Outcome.description: How a run ended, as its runner saw it.

oneOf.description: `fingerprint` is the error class + step, for the loop breaker.
Usage reached the run's token cap.
No progress for `RunLimits.stall_after_secs` (1.14): the runner stopped it.

Output.description: Bytes on a stream (exec output later, terminal `out`/`in`), standard base64.

oneOf.description: Everything outside the allowlist asks.
File edits inside the run's directory go ahead; the rest asks.
The harness acts without asking. Only with `sandboxed`.

Policy.description: A project's harness permission policy (1.3). Never full-auto by default.

allow.description:
Tools the harness may use without asking: a tool name (`Edit`, `fileChange`), or
`<tool>:<command prefix>` (`Bash:cargo test`) for a command with no shell operators, or a
chain of commands each of which it covers.

sandboxed.description: Runs must work in a disposable sandbox: only a sandboxed runner may take them.

Reply.description: Runner to Core, a command's last frame when it ran.

oneOf.description: An op from a newer runner. Never sent.

RepoDiff.description: One repo's worktree against its base (1.18): `git diff --numstat` plus untracked files.

insertions.description: Lines added (an untracked text file's every line) and removed.

repo.description: The repo's name in its project; empty for an issue's only repo.

Route.description: One entry of an agent's fallback chain (E15.3), with the account picked for it.

RunLimits.description: What the runner is told of the server's settings for one run (1.11, E15.17).

approval_timeout_secs.description: How long an escalated tool call waits for a reviewer before it is denied.

fallback_on_model_unavailable.description:
Whether a turn failing for this class moves the run to the next entry of its fallback
chain (1.20); otherwise the run fails. Absent from an older server: it does.

max_resumes.description: Resumes of a dropped session before the run gives up on its model (E15.4).

resume_backoff_ms.description: The first wait before a resume, doubling per drop, and the longest.

stall_after_secs.description:
How long the run may go without progress before it is stopped as stalled (1.14,
E15.7). Absent from an older server: `STALL_AFTER_SECS`.

tool_output_bytes.description:
The most of a tool's output a `tool_result` transcript event carries (1.18). Absent
from an older server: `TOOL_OUTPUT_BYTES`.

warm_max.description:
Idle harness servers the runner keeps for later runs (1.13, E15.6); 0, none. Absent
from an older server: none.

RunToken.description:
A run token on the wire. Its `Debug` is redacted, so logging a message never logs it;
`expose` is the one way to read it.

drivers.description: What it can run. The Core sends only commands listed here.

protocol.description: `PROTOCOL_VERSION` of the runner; the Core refuses a major it does not speak.

RunnerInfo.description: What a runner says of itself (1.20).

logins.description:
Each harness and account config dir (and account token file) it found, and whether it
is logged in there.

power_nap.description: The Power Nap preference it holds, as the server last sent it.

slept_secs.description: How long its machine last slept, if it slept since the daemon started.

RunnerLimits.description:
What the runner is told of the server's settings for it (1.15, E15.9, decision #57: server-wide
per runner, not per company).

disk_cap_bytes.description: The most its work root may hold: worktrees, shared build caches and repo mirrors.

disk_evict_percent.description: Share of the cap past which idle worktrees are evicted, oldest first, then caches.

warm_idle_secs.description: How long a warm harness server may sit idle before it is stopped (E15.6).

workspace_idle_secs.description:
How long a worktree may sit with no run before it is removed (its work kept on its
branch, uncommitted changes on `refs/citadel/wip/<issue>`), recreated on demand.

StreamError.description: A command's failure, or (on stream 0) a connection's. `message` is human text, redacted.

TokenCaps.description:
A run's caps, split (1.27): what the runner counts its tokens against. A run stops when
either applies. Its tokens are counted from its events, and the caps stay exact for the
budgets and the issue; only `run` is weighted.

cache_weight_divisor.description: How much a cache token counts against `run`, as a divisor (1: every token in full).

exact.description:
The least left in the budgets and the issue's cap that apply, counted in full (0 is
stop at once); absent when none applies.

run.description:
`run.token_cap`, compared with the run's tokens where cache reads and writes count at
`1 / cache_weight_divisor` (0 is stop at once).

Tokens.description: Token counts. A cap counts their `sum`.

cost_usd_micros.description:
What the harness itself says the run has cost so far, in millionths of a US dollar,
when it says (Claude's `total_cost_usd`, OpenCode's session cost; 1.6). Not part of
`sum`. Absent: the server prices the tokens, or leaves them unpriced.

V2Payload.description: A v2 Frame's payload by kind: control Control, command Command, result Reply, error StreamError, output Output, credit Credit, close Close, heartbeat none.

Workspace.description: Where an issue's run works: a git worktree of `repo` on `branch`, cut from `base`.

also.description: The issue's other repos, in its project's order, when it touches several (1.16).

expected_head.description:
The sha the branch was last pushed at (1.28), `None` before its first push. The runner
leases its push on it, so a rewritten branch lands only over the head it last saw.

name.description: The repo's name in its project (1.16): its worktree's directory in a multi-repo workspace.

push.description:
Push the branch to the repo's origin when the run ends (1.7): its project is on a forge,
where a PR is opened from it (E9.1).

repo.description: A URL or path git can clone, never holding credentials (`repo_url_problem`).

active.description: A run is using it: never evicted.

idle_secs.description: Seconds since a run last used it.

description: RunnerMessage: runner to server (v1). ServerMessage: server to runner (v1). Frame: either way (v2, multiplexed streams).

oneOf.description: Runner → server.
The first message of every connection.

disk.description: Its last disk report (1.15), if it made one.

harnesses.description:
Installed harness → version, e.g. `claude` → `2.1.306`, from its `--version` (or
`unknown (…)` when unreadable). A version at or above the adapter's minimum and not
known bad gets work (1.21); a refused one marks the runner unhealthy (E3.6).

info.description: Its state (1.20); absent from an older runner.

os.description: Its operating system and CPU architecture (1.25), e.g. `macos` and `aarch64`.

runs.description: Runs it is still working on, to resume after a reconnect.

oneOf.description: The answer to `Probe` `request` (1.25): what it found now.

error.description: Why it could not look, if it could not.

oneOf.description: Its state, after each clean-up pass (1.20).

The answer to `ReadLog` `request` (1.20): the last lines of its log, redacted, or why
not.
Its disk use after a clean-up pass (1.15, E15.9).

It has a free slot and wants one run. `workspaces`: the issues it holds a worktree
for (1.1).
It is still working on `run`; `load` (1.26) is the host's load when it says.

`run` progressed (1.14): a tool call, a file change, a new message or more tokens.
`diff_files`: how many files its worktree differs from the base in, when measured.

repos.description:
Each repo's diff against its base, in the issue's repo order (1.18); empty when not
measured.

oneOf.description: The harness for `run` is up; `session` is its resumable session id, if it has one.

One transcript chunk, numbered from 1 per run, redacted (`redact`). The server stores
each `seq` once; a resend is ignored.

The run's token totals so far, numbered from 1 per run (1.2). Totals, not deltas: a
lost or repeated report loses or double-counts nothing.

The harness asks for a tool call the run's policy does not allow (1.3). `id` is the
harness's request id, unique within the run; `input` is redacted. Resent after a
reconnect until answered; the server keeps one approval per `(run, id)`.
The run moved to the next entry of its fallback chain (1.9): `harness` and `model` as
in the `Assign`'s `fallbacks`, working as `account`; `class` is why (`model_unavailable`,
`rate_limited`, `quota`, `no_account`), `reason` the harness's words, redacted.

The provider dropped the run's turn and the runner resumes its session (1.10). Not
resent: a drop lost to a dropped connection is not counted.

timeout_secs.description:
How long the runner waits before denying it (1.5), so the server expires the
approval at the same moment. Absent from an older runner: the server's deadline.

oneOf.description:
The answer to `ReadFile` `request` (1.17): the file's bytes in standard base64, or why
it was not read.
Server → runner.

limits.description: Its disk and warm-process settings (1.15); absent, the runner's defaults.

power_nap.description: The admin's Power Nap preference for it (1.20); absent, none set.

oneOf.description: A claimed run for the runner to start. Holds no secret.

account.description: The provider account to work as (1.8); absent, the runner's own harness login.

context_ref.description: Where the run's context is read, through the Citadel MCP server (E4.2).

fallbacks.description: The rest of the agent's fallback chain, in order (1.9).

instructions.description:
The run's skills rendered as markdown, for the harness's instructions file (1.4,
E4.3); absent when the run has none.

issue_key.description: The issue's key, e.g. `CIT-12`, for the prompt (1.4).

limits.description: The run's limits from the server's settings (1.11); absent, the runner's defaults.

policy.description: The project's permission policy (1.3); absent, the default (ask).

prompt.description:
The run's first turn (1.22): its job on this wake and its done rule; absent, the
runner's own.

resume_session.description:
A session of the run's harness to continue rather than starting a new one (1.12,
E15.5); absent, a fresh session.

token_cap.description:
Tokens the run may use: the least left in any budget that applies, or the
server's default (1.2). Absent from an older server: the runner's default.

token_caps.description:
The run's caps split (1.27), see `TokenCaps`; absent from an older server, which
sends `token_cap` alone.

workspace.description: The issue's git worktree, when its project has a repo (1.1).

oneOf.description:
The started run's token, for the harness to call back with. Sent once per start or
re-start (a resumed `RunStarted` rotates it).

Stop and forget `run`: it was cancelled, ended already, or this runner no longer holds
it. Send no `RunEnded`.
`RunEnded` for `run` was recorded.

The answer to `ApprovalRequest` `id` of `run` (1.3): `reply` is the reviewer's note,
which a denial passes to the agent as its reason.
Finish the tool call in flight, then stop `run`'s turn and end it `Cancelled` (1.19).
The admin's message `id` for `run`'s harness, given to it as its next turn (1.19).
Remove the worktrees of these issues: they are done, cancelled or gone (1.1).

Read `path`, relative to `run`'s worktree, of at most `max_bytes` (1.17); answered by
`FileRead`.
The last `lines` lines of the runner's own log (1.20); answered by `LogTail`.
The admin changed its Power Nap preference (1.20).
Look at yourself again now (1.25); answered by `Probed`.
`run`'s permission policy changed (1.24): its next tool calls are decided by `policy`.
A message was refused for a reason other than the run: a protocol or storage error.

title: Ainkrad runner protocol
